11.actor: a debtor, his purchaser and his creditor
11.event: the debtor sold two plots for fifty each; the creditor seized one and came for the other
11.turn: the purchaser took a hundred dinars to the creditor
11.outcome: offered: take the plot as worth a hundred, or take the hundred and leave both plots

15.event: his father sent him up to fetch chicks; he sent away the mother bird and took the young
15.turn: on his way down he fell
15.outcome: he died, despite two mitzvot promising long life
15.summary: A father told his son to climb up and bring him chicks. The son climbed, sent away the mother bird and took the young, fulfilling two mitzvot promising long life, yet on returning he fell and died. Rabbi Ya'akov concludes the promised reward is in the World-to-Come.
15.reason: A narrated sequence of actions with a reversal and outcome, which the context says Rabbi Ya'akov witnessed; the Gemara's doubts in the following segment are commentary, excluded.

16.actor: Rabban Gamliel, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Akiva
16.event: returning from Pelandarsin, their boat sailed out on Shabbat
16.turn: two walked the whole boat while two stayed within four cubits
16.outcome: the two were stringent with themselves
16.summary: Four sages were sailing from Pelandarsin when their boat put out to sea on Shabbat. Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya walked about the whole boat, while Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva did not move beyond four cubits, choosing stringency.
16.reason: A Mishnah incident quoted by the Gemara (R-C1) with several actors and actions in a one-time event; though causality is modest, it is a narrated incident of sages.
